key_insight: C2FMAE resolves the trade-off between global semantics and local textures by learning hierarchical visual representations with a coarse-to-fine masked autoencoder that moves from scene-level semantic masks to fine pixel reconstruction.
problem_solved: Self-supervised visual pretraining methods either capture global semantics (contrastive learning) or local textures (masked image modeling); random masking in MIM causes attention drift and fails to preserve semantics. This paper addresses how to jointly learn both levels without semantic-agnostic masking.
method: Generate semantically-aware coarse masks (scene-level) and progressively refine to instance-level and pixel/patch-level masks for masking and reconstruction.
Train a masked autoencoder in a coarse-to-fine curriculum so the model first captures global structure and then recovers instance details and local textures.
Use multi-granularity reconstruction objectives (and/or auxiliary semantic consistency losses) to align global semantics with fine-grained pixel prediction and reduce attention drift.
impact: Provides a practical pretraining strategy that preserves both high-level semantics and low-level details, improving transfer performance on downstream vision tasks (classification, detection, segmentation) and making representations more robust and interpretable.

paper_title: From Semantics to Pixels: Coarse-to-Fine Masked Autoencoders for Hierarchical Visual Understanding
paper_authors: Wenzhao Xiang, Yue Wu, Hongyang Yu, Feng Gao, Fan Yang
